process_area.title: Supply Chain Human Rights Risk Assessment, Auditing & Remediation

value_stream.name: Human Rights, Modern Slavery & Responsible Supply Chain Due Diligence

fields.Participants: Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-122), Sustainability, Global Sourcing (links to VS-122), Legal, third-party risk-data providers

workflows.name: Supplier Human Rights Risk Assessment & Tiering

Automation Opportunity: - System continuous audit of "Procurement/Sustainability conduct the supplier human-rights risk assessment using the" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-track of "Procurement/Sustainability tier each supplier" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - operational: multi-input assessment and refresh; operational: audit of high-risk suppliers
Pain Points / Risks: - **Tiering-error risk**: High-risk supplier mis-tiered low; mitigated by multi-input assessment and refresh
- **Questionnaire-only risk**: Self-assessment gaming; mitigated by audit of high-risk suppliers
System Touchpoints: - Procurement/vendor (links to VS-03/VS-122/VS-67); MDM (links to VS-29); ABC/sanctions (links to VS-86); ESG (links to VS-25); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: Procurement/Sustainability conduct the supplier human-rights risk assessment using the model (W4006), geography/category risk, questionnaire (self-assessment), certifications, media/NGO/sanctions screening (links to VS-86), and prior-audit history

Procurement/Sustainability tier each supplier (low / enhanced / high) and define the DD intensity: low = self-assessment + code; enhanced = audit/capability; high = enhanced audit + traceability + remediation tracking
Procurement integrate tiering into vendor master (links to VS-29) and scorecard (links to VS-67), trigger audits (W4010), and refresh on cycle or event

fields.Frequency: Per cycle (1–3 years by risk) + on trigger
fields.Participants: Sustainability, Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-122), accredited third-party social auditors (SMETA/SA8000/amfori BSCI), Global Sourcing (links to VS-122), Compliance

workflows.name: Social Compliance Audit, Verification & Capability Building

Automation Opportunity: - System continuous audit of "audits for high/enhanced-risk vendors/factories" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "review audit findings, verify accuracy" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "Sustainability/Procurement build supplier capability" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-624 (ensure controlled execution — Supply Chain Human Rights Risk Assessment, Auditing & Remediation (PA-131.2).)
- operational: unannounced audits and worker voice; operational: capability building and closure tracking
Pain Points / Risks: - **Audit-fraud risk**: Findings concealed or coached; mitigated by unannounced audits and worker voice
- **Tick-box-audit risk**: Audit without improvement; mitigated by capability building and closure tracking
System Touchpoints: - Procurement/vendor (links to VS-03/VS-122/VS-67); ESG (links to VS-25); audit (links to VS-21); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: Sustainability/Procurement plan and commission accredited third-party social-compliance audits for high/enhanced-risk vendors/factories (labor, health & safety, environment, ethics, management systems), unannounced/semi-announced where warranted
Sustainability review audit findings, verify accuracy (links to W4011 worker voice), classify non-conformances (critical/major/minor), and issue corrective-action requirements (links to W4012)

Sustainability/Procurement build supplier capability (training, toolkits, peer benchmarking), track closure (W4012), and integrate outcomes into the scorecard (links to VS-67) and sourcing decisions (W4014)

fields.Participants: Sustainability, Procurement, external assessors, worker-voice technology providers, local stakeholders
fields.Trigger: High-risk audit; worker-grievance signal; direct assessment need

workflows.name: On-Site Assessment, Worker Voice & Grievance Verification

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "Sustainability/external-assessors conduct on-site assessment beyond paperwork" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-log of "Sustainability deploy/leverage worker-voice channels" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "verify audit vs worker-voice vs documents, investigate discrepancies, and feed…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-624 (ensure controlled execution — Supply Chain Human Rights Risk Assessment, Auditing & Remediation (PA-131.2).)
- operational: worker-voice interviews conducted on-site with confidentiality safeguards and retaliation monitoring via the grievance channel
Pain Points / Risks: - **Document-only risk**: Audits verifying documents not reality; mitigated by worker voice and on-site verification
- **Retaliation risk**: Workers punished for speaking up; mitigated by confidentiality and retaliation monitoring
System Touchpoints: - Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-122); ESG (links to VS-25); ethics/speak-up (links to VS-119); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: Sustainability/external-assessors conduct on-site assessment beyond paperwork: worker interviews (confidential, multiple shifts), document verification (payroll, age/ID, hours), and physical inspection (safety, dormitories where relevant)

Sustainability deploy/leverage worker-voice channels (anonymous surveys, hotlines, technology tools) to verify audit findings and surface hidden issues (forced-labor indicators, harassment, wage/hour violations)
Sustainability cross-verify audit vs worker-voice vs documents, investigate discrepancies, and feed verified findings into corrective action (W4012) and grievance remediation (W4013)

fields.Participants: Sustainability, Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-67/VS-122), affected vendor, Compliance, Legal (links to VS-100), affected workers/community

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-issue of "issue corrective-action plans" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-validate of "Sustainability/Procurement track CAP closure, verify remediation" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "document remediation outcomes, and feed into sourcing decisions" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-624 (ensure controlled execution — Supply Chain Human Rights Risk Assessment, Auditing & Remediation (PA-131.2).)
- operational: tracking and sourcing consequences (W4014); operational: verification and worker confirmation
Pain Points / Risks: - **Non-closure risk**: CAPs open indefinitely; mitigated by tracking and sourcing consequences (W4014)
- **Incomplete-remedy risk**: Workers not made whole; mitigated by verification and worker confirmation
System Touchpoints: - Procurement/vendor (links to VS-03/VS-67/VS-122); legal (links to VS-100); ESG (links to VS-25); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: Sustainability issue corrective-action plans (CAPs) per finding with root cause, required remediation (e.g., back-pay, reimbursement of recruitment fees, safety fixes, age-verification systems), owner, and deadline; require supplier commitment

Sustainability/Procurement track CAP closure, verify remediation (re-payment evidence, re-inspection, worker confirmation), and address systemic causes (management systems); escalate critical/major findings
Sustainability provide/leverage remedy for affected workers/community, document remediation outcomes, and feed into sourcing decisions (W4014), reporting (W4020), and continuous improvement (W4019)

fields.Participants: Sustainability, Compliance (links to VS-119), Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-122), Legal, external grievance-channel providers, affected workers
fields.Trigger: Worker grievance via channel; allegation/media/NGO report

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "Sustainability triage, investigate" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-monitor of "monitor for retaliation, and report aggregated grievance data" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-624 (ensure controlled execution — Supply Chain Human Rights Risk Assessment, Auditing & Remediation (PA-131.2).)
- operational: accessibility and communication; operational: confidentiality and retaliation monitoring
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-use risk**: Workers don't trust/aren't aware of channels; mitigated by accessibility and communication
- **Retaliation risk**: Workers punished for grievance; mitigated by confidentiality and retaliation monitoring
System Touchpoints: - Ethics/speak-up (links to VS-119); procurement (links to VS-03/VS-122); ESG (links to VS-25); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: Sustainability/Compliance operate accessible supply-chain grievance channels (hotline, app, worker-committee) for workers in BuildRight's supply chain, ensuring accessibility (language, literacy), confidentiality, and non-retaliation — distinct from BuildRight's own speak-up (VS-119)
Sustainability triage, investigate (with supplier cooperation), and verify grievances; coordinate with audits (W4010/W4011) and CAPs (W4012)
Sustainability provide remedy, monitor for retaliation, and report aggregated grievance data (W4020); engage stakeholders where systemic (W4021)

fields.Participants: Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-122/VS-67), Sustainability, Merchandising (links to VS-01), Legal (links to VS-100), Supply Planning (links to VS-02), Compliance
fields.Trigger: Uncorrected critical finding; unremediated abuse; sourcing decision

workflows.name: Sourcing Decision, Pause & Exit (Responsible Disengagement) Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "document the decision basis" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-624 (ensure controlled execution — Supply Chain Human Rights Risk Assessment, Auditing & Remediation (PA-131.2).)
- operational: UNGP leverage-first principle; operational: phased approach and alternatives
Pain Points / Risks: - **Reflexive-exit risk**: Disengagement harming workers more than helping; mitigated by UNGP leverage-first principle
- **Supply-shock risk**: Exit disrupting supply; mitigated by phased approach and alternatives
System Touchpoints: - Procurement/supply planning (links to VS-03/VS-02/VS-122/VS-67); merchandising (links to VS-01); legal (links to VS-100); governance (links to VS-36); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: Procurement/Sustainability integrate human-rights performance into sourcing decisions: prefer compliant/improving suppliers; pause new orders for unremediated critical findings; and weigh responsible disengagement as a last resort per UNGP (leverage, not reflexive exit)

Procurement/Sustainability manage responsible exit where required: phased disengagement, mitigate harm to workers (avoid sudden mass job loss), source alternatives (links to VS-122/VS-03), and protect supply continuity (links to VS-02)

Procurement/Sustainability document the decision basis (links to VS-88), report to governance/Board (links to VS-36/W4017), and apply lessons to risk model (W4006) and sourcing strategy (links to VS-122)

fields.Participants: Sustainability, Procurement/Global Sourcing (links to VS-03/VS-122), Merchandising (links to VS-01), Insights, external mineral-DD providers, Legal
fields.Volume: Mineral-intensive categories (tools, power tools, electronics, appliances)

workflows.name: Conflict Minerals, Responsible Materials & Smelter Due Diligence

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Sustainability report on minerals DD" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-624 (ensure controlled execution — Supply Chain Human Rights Risk Assessment, Auditing & Remediation (PA-131.2).)
- operational: smelter identification and RMAP; operational: a single CMRT/EMRT process
Pain Points / Risks: - **Origin-blindness risk**: Minerals sourced from conflict areas; mitigated by smelter identification and RMAP
- **Reporting-burden risk**: B2B customers cascading mineral requests; mitigated by a single CMRT/EMRT process
System Touchpoints: - Procurement/global sourcing (links to VS-03/VS-122); merchandising (links to VS-01); ABC/sanctions (links to VS-86); anti-counterfeit (links to VS-71); ESG (links to VS-25); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: Sustainability/Procurement scope mineral exposure in BuildRight's assortment (3TG — tin/tungsten/tantalum/gold — and cobalt/mica in tools/electronics/appliances/PPE) and apply the OECD Due Diligence Guidance for Responsible Supply Chains of Minerals from Conflict-Affected and High-Risk Areas

Procurement require smelter/refiner identification (CMRT/EMRT), prefer responsibly-assured smelters (RMAP), and trace to origin where feasible; integrate with global sourcing (links to VS-122.2) and the broader responsible-materials program
Sustainability report on minerals DD (links to W4020), engage stakeholders (W4021), and refresh on sourcing change; coordinate with sanctions (links to VS-86) and anti-counterfeit (links to VS-71)

fields.Participants: Sustainability, Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-122), Insights, external wage-benchmark providers, HR (links to VS-102 for own-ops parity)

workflows.name: Living Wage, Working Hours & Wage-Data Assurance Program

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-identify of "identify categories/geographies of concern" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System continuous audit of "work with suppliers on closing living-wage gaps" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report progress (links to W4020)" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-624 (ensure controlled execution — Supply Chain Human Rights Risk Assessment, Auditing & Remediation (PA-131.2).)
- operational: living-wage benchmarking; operational: hour-data assurance and audit
Pain Points / Risks: - **Wage-gap risk**: Legal-minimum compliance masking sub-living wages; mitigated by living-wage benchmarking
- **Hours-abuse risk**: Excessive/forced overtime; mitigated by hour-data assurance and audit
System Touchpoints: - Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-122); insights (links to VS-44); compensation (links to VS-102); audit (links to VS-21); ESG (links to VS-25)

steps.activity: Sustainability/Procurement assess living-wage gaps and working-hours compliance in high-risk supplier geographies using living-wage benchmarks (vs legal minimum) and hour/wage data, and identify categories/geographies of concern

Procurement/Sustainability work with suppliers on closing living-wage gaps (wage ladders, pricing that supports legal/living wage) and hours compliance (no excessive overtime, voluntary overtime), verified via audit (W4010) and wage-data assurance
Sustainability report progress (links to W4020), engage stakeholders (W4021), and align with BuildRight's own compensation philosophy (links to VS-102) and worker-voice (W4013)
